purpose: Generate new practice prompts from existing verified graph relationships and failure modes without inventing SAP behavior.

generation_patterns.template: Start with a documented failure symptom. Ask the learner to build a hypothesis tree, identify the first wrong layer, and define proof of cause.
Take a documented ownership boundary and make both adjacent domains look locally correct while the end-to-end result is wrong. Ask who owns the first correction.
Take a downstream symptom and require the learner to trace backwards through two or more runtime stages before changing the final document.
Take a valid design rule and change one condition such as volume, legal constraint, ordering need, deployment model, or recovery requirement. Ask whether the original design still holds.
Join two or more graphs through a shared business event, document, value, or integration boundary. Ask for an end-to-end completion proof.

quality_rules: Every factual expected point must be supported by the referenced graph or its source registry.
Do not invent transaction codes, tables, message types, configuration paths, or product behavior that is absent from the evidence.
Synthetic business data is allowed, but label the scenario as synthetic when published outside the assessment dataset.
A Lead case should contain at least one ownership boundary, failure proof, or trade-off. Pure terminology questions are rejected.
Avoid cases where the answer is one product name or one transaction code.
Prefer a clear first wrong decision over a long list of unrelated checks.

deduplication.rule: Reject a generated case when its normalized title, symptom, graph_refs, and expected_points substantially overlap an existing case.
deduplication.minimum_new_signal: At least one new boundary, failure path, or reasoning-level challenge must be present.
